title: European Parliament Passes Resolution Backing Spanish Sovereignty Over Ceuta, Calls Crossing 'Hybrid Warfare'
detail: MEPs adopted a non-binding resolution on the Ceuta crisis by 339 votes to 225, with 16 abstentions, describing the July 30-31 mass crossing as an 'instrumentalisation of irregular migration' and framing it within a broader 'hybrid warfare' narrative, while demanding 'unconditional respect for the territorial integrity of EU countries' and stating that any challenge to Spanish sovereignty is 'unacceptable and incompatible with the obligations of a partner country.' The text also criticised aspects of Spain's own migration policy as a 'pull factor.' Ceuta president Juan Jesús Vivas called the vote an 'important endorsement' of the city, welcoming its recognition of Ceuta as a model of coexistence. Morocco's ambassador to the EU and NATO, Ahmed Reda Chami, pushed back, saying the resolution contains 'no condemnation or injunction' against Rabat and 'does not endorse any of the attempts to instrumentalize the migration crisis.' Separately, Spanish ministers Elma Saiz and Fernando Grande-Marlaska met EU Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner the same day to discuss the crisis at EU level.

media.caption: Morocco's EU/NATO ambassador says the European Parliament's Ceuta resolution contains no condemnation of Rabat

title: Two Soldiers Evacuated to Madrid Hospital After Separate Assaults During Ceuta Deployment
detail: Spain's Defense Ministry confirmed the evacuation of two soldiers injured during their Ceuta deployment to the Hospital Central de la Defensa Gómez Ulla in Madrid. One, from the Ceuta Regulares group, suffered a knee injury — initially described as a dislocation, later requiring surgery for a fractured fibula — after an incident on Sep 9; the second sustained a shoulder injury in a separate attack around 4am on Sep 12 in the Juan XXIII area. Defense Minister Margarita Robles visited both soldiers in hospital on Sep 17; the ministry said in a statement 'our soldiers [are] always professional, close to and involved with Ceuta.' The incidents add to a string of assaults on security forces deployed since the July 30-31 crossing.
